title: UPI Transaction Limits Explained: From ₹1 Lakh to ₹5 Lakh
description: The standard daily UPI transaction limit for most payments is ₹1 lakh per bank account. Certain specific categories, like payments to hospitals and educationa.

faq.q: What is the standard daily UPI transaction limit?
faq.a: The standard daily UPI transaction limit for most general payments is ₹1 lakh per bank account. This applies to peer-to-peer transfers and merchant payments for everyday purchases.

faq.q: Are there higher UPI limits for specific types of payments?
faq.a: Yes, for certain categories like payments to hospitals, educational institutions, tax payments, and subscriptions to Initial Public Offerings (IPOs) or Mutual Funds, the UPI limit is enhanced to ₹5 lakh.

faq.q: Can my bank set lower UPI transaction limits than the NPCI?
faq.a: Yes, while NPCI sets the maximum limits, individual banks have the discretion to impose lower daily or per-transaction limits for their customers. It's advisable to check your bank's specific policies.

faq.q: Is there a limit on the number of UPI transactions I can make in a day?
faq.a: While there isn't a strict universal limit on the *number* of transactions, exceeding a certain frequency might flag your account for review by your bank. The primary constraint is the aggregate daily monetary limit.

faq.q: Do merchant payments have different UPI limits?
faq.a: For most retail merchant payments, the standard ₹1 lakh daily limit applies. However, specific merchant categories like hospitals or educational institutions are eligible for the enhanced ₹5 lakh limit.

faq.q: How do UPI limits affect IPO applications?
faq.a: You can apply for IPOs via UPI with a limit of up to ₹5 lakh. This allows retail investors to subscribe to larger amounts directly through their UPI-enabled apps.

faq.q: What happens if I try to exceed my UPI limit?
faq.a: If you attempt a transaction that exceeds your daily or per-transaction limit, the payment will typically fail, and you will receive an error message from your bank or UPI app.
